title: Literature positioning for the one-dimensional impurity benchmark
status_detail: The human response `A` at RM-IMPURITY-DEFECT-1D-LITERATURE-POSITIONING-ACCEPTANCE-HC01 accepts the bounded primary-literature positioning, conservative contribution statement, and project-local review-method record. The retained review covers 15 claim-level primary sources, distinguishes full-text from abstract-level support, labels two 2026 records as preprints, and limits the contribution to an integrated reproducible diagnostic synthesis rather than a new component theorem, priority claim, material result, scientific validation, or continuum proof. The claim matrix, bibliography, manuscript, checkpoint, Harness state, generated projections, and diff checks pass. No material calculation, external scientific execution, dependency change, successor activation, publication submission, or release is accepted or authorized.
objective: Position the accepted baseline and completed one-dimensional follow-on experiments against verified primary literature without overstating novelty, material validity, or continuum conclusions.
authorized_scope: Identify and verify primary sources for retained-space alignment, Wannier or localized-basis Hamiltonian differences, impurity operators, finite-rank spectral methods, supercell image effects, and envelope or effective-mass limits.

Compare the benchmark's definitions, controls, failure modes, and evidence boundary with the verified literature, distinguishing established methods from the contribution of the integrated reproducible exercise.
Update Appendix I and its bibliography with claim-level attribution, unresolved citation notes, and a conservative novelty statement.

Begin from, but do not limit the search to, Koster--Slater finite-rank impurity methods; Simon and Parzygnat--Lee--Avniel--Johnson weak-binding or localization results; Hoefer--Weinstein and Duchene--Vukicevic--Weinstein band-edge homogenization; Nakamura--Tadano discrete-to-continuum convergence; Koenig--Lee--Hammer finite-volume bound-state analysis; and Kohn--Luttinger and Gamble et al. semiconductor effective-mass, central-cell, and multivalley boundaries.

Distinguish continuum numerical-grid refinement, physical lattice-scale refinement, weak slowly varying band-edge scaling, finite-volume refinement, and changes of defect profile or normalization; determine source applicability separately for each limit.
completion_criteria: Every substantive positioning claim is supported by an identified and checked primary source or remains explicitly marked unresolved.
The resulting prose distinguishes methodological integration and reproducibility from new physics, a new alignment theorem, material validation, or a new localization algorithm.
Bibliographic metadata, quotations if any, and the final claim boundary are independently checked and the manuscript builds without warnings.

A claim-to-source matrix records, for every cited methodological precedent, the operator class, dimension, scaling parameter, state-space identification, spectral regime, defect assumptions, finite-volume assumptions, conclusion, and mismatch with the project's represented benchmark.

The final positioning states that established component methods do not by themselves establish this benchmark's continuum crossover, material validity, or novelty; any contribution claim is limited to what remains after the full primary-source comparison.
exclusions: Bibliography presence alone does not establish that a source supports a claim.
No novelty, priority, material transferability, scientific validation, publication acceptance, or release claim may be inferred from the synthetic exercises.
No material calculation, external scientific execution, dependency change, publication submission, or release action is authorized.
